name: Fuzhou Streets 2014 vs 2020: Which Looks Happier? (Older Adults)
description:
Method replication: older adults compare 30 pairs of street views from central Fuzhou and click the one that looks happier; the pool mixes the same street points as photographed around 2014 and around 2020, as in the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (94 re-fetched Baidu street views at 47 points inside the Third Ring Road, one view per point and year, heading 0° or 270° as in the paper).

Original study: Guo, Wan, Li, Li, Yin & Ho (2025), Building and Environment 284, 113410. 250 adults aged 60–75, recruited in Fuzhou parks and screened for eye conditions, answered "which image looks happier" on an online platform. Images came in groups of 14 (seven points, each in 2014 and 2020), and every image was compared with the other 13 in its group: 22,750 comparisons over 3,500 Baidu street views. TrueSkill scores were related to the 3D morphology of street trees with nonlinear machine learning.

Differences from the original study: (1) newly fetched Baidu street views from the nearest available years (2014 and 2019–2021) instead of the authors' images, which are not released; (2) 30 random pairs from the whole pool instead of all 91 pairs within one group of 14 images; (3) the eye-condition screening is asked as a question rather than checked in person, and gender, age and residence are asked first.
author: Guo, Wan, Li, Li, Yin & Ho
